exposure: Clinical assessment via digital examination (cervical dilatation, fetal head station, fetal head position)
Transperineal ultrasonographic measurements (cervical dilatation, angle of progression, head-perineum distance, fetal head position)
outcome: Agreement between sonographic measurements and digital examinations
cohort: The study included 43 women in labor at a tertiary care center in Turkey.
finding: The study found good agreement between clinical and ultrasound assessment of cervical dilatation, moderate agreement for fetal head station, and low agreement for fetal head position.
